transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… what finally made me come in is that I don’t really feel like myself anymore. I used to always have things I cared about—painting, going hiking, choir practice, Sunday dinners with my family. I was the one who made sure people showed up, actually.

And now, even if I have a free hour, I just kind of sit there. I think about getting out the paints or calling someone, and it’s like… I can’t make myself care. It sounds small when I say it, but it doesn’t feel small.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?

Yes… most days, I think. It’s not always like I’m openly crying or anything, though sometimes I feel close to it. It’s more like there’s this heavy gray film over everything.

I can be in the classroom with the kids around me, or at home with my husband, and I still feel sort of hollow. Like I’m there, but I’m not really… there. And then I’ll catch myself thinking about something completely ordinary, like whether we’re out of milk, and suddenly I feel like I might cry. It’s strange.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It’s been… about eight months, I think. It kind of started building around when I took over the STEM-Arts curriculum initiative at school.

At first I thought I was just tired from that, because there were so many meetings and everyone had opinions about glue guns and coding stations and—sorry. But yes, about eight months. It’s gotten harder to shake since then.
Do these feelings seem mostly connected to the stress from taking on the curriculum initiative?

I thought it was just that at first, because it did start around when I took over the STEM-Arts curriculum thing. It’s been building for about eight months now.

But… I don’t know, it’s hard to separate. That project was such a mess—everyone had a different opinion, and we had all these supply lists and parent emails and scheduling meetings—and I kept thinking, “Once this settles down, I’ll feel better.” But it didn’t really settle, or I didn’t. It just kept sort of… accumulating.
Has this been making it hard for you to function at work or at home?

Yes… it has. More than I wanted to admit, honestly.

At work I’ve missed several teaching sessions, which I never used to do. And I’ve been avoiding the student workshops because I just can’t seem to keep up with all the responsibilities the way I used to. Even the setup feels overwhelming sometimes—bins of markers, sign-in sheets, all the little pieces that used to be kind of fun.

And at home… my husband has had to step in more. I’ll say I’m going to come to something, like a family plan or dinner, and then I just sort of withdraw. I don’t always feel safe pushing through on my own, if that makes sense. Like I might fall apart if I try to keep pretending I’m fine.
Before these past eight months, was there ever another period in your life when you felt depressed like this for at least two weeks?

I’m not sure. I mean… I’ve had low stretches before, like anyone, I guess. There were times when things felt heavy, especially around stressful school years or family stuff, and I’d sort of pull inward.

But whether it was like this, for at least two weeks straight… I don’t know. I don’t think I’ve ever really tracked it that way. I’m sorry, I’m probably not answering clearly. It’s hard for me to separate “I was tired and overwhelmed” from “I was really depressed,” if that makes sense.
Have you had trouble sleeping lately?

Yes… my sleep has been really all over the place for months now. I’ll get into bed and then my brain starts going through grant details, or supply lists, or some email I forgot to answer—sometimes it’s not even important, but it feels urgent at two in the morning.

And then I wake up around three or four a lot. It’s that horrible kind of awake where you know you need more sleep, but your mind is already running. Even on nights when I technically sleep longer, I wake up feeling like I didn’t really rest at all.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of harming yourself?

Yes… um. I don’t like saying this, but yes, I’ve had thoughts like that.

It’s mostly late at night, especially if I’m in the studio and everything is quiet and I’m just sitting there with all the mess around me—paint cups and paper scraps and half-finished things—and I’ll catch myself thinking it would be a relief if I just didn’t wake up. Not like I’ve sat down and made a plan, I haven’t… but the thoughts scared me.

I told my husband because I felt like I couldn’t keep handling it by myself.
Before this current eight-month period, was there ever another time in your life when you felt depressed nearly every day for at least two weeks?

I really don’t know. I keep trying to think back and it all gets blurry, like… was I sad every day, or was I just stressed and shutting down?

There were times I remember being kind of withdrawn, especially when work or family things piled up, and I’d get quieter for a while. But I can’t honestly say, “yes, it was nearly every day for two weeks.” I didn’t pay attention to it that way then.

So… maybe? But I’m not sure enough to say.
Before this current eight-month period, was there ever a time in your life when you felt depressed nearly every day for at least two months?

I’m not sure… two months feels like such a specific stretch to try to remember.

I mean, I’ve had periods where I was really low or sort of not myself, but then life was also busy and messy, and I’d tell myself it was just work stress or family stuff. Like, I remember certain semesters feeling endless, especially when everyone needed something at once, and I’d just kind of keep going because you have to.

But whether I was depressed nearly every day for two full months before this? I honestly don’t know. I can’t say that clearly.
If the problems with the curriculum initiative suddenly went away, do you think you would still feel depressed?

I think… yes. I mean, the curriculum thing makes everything worse, definitely, and I get so worked up about it because it feels like nobody understands how much extra it’s asking of us.

But even if that disappeared tomorrow, I don’t think I’d suddenly feel normal. Most days it’s like there’s this heavy gray film over everything. I can be in the classroom with students all around me, or at home with my husband, and still feel kind of hollow… like I’m right on the edge of crying for no clear reason.

So, yes. I think I’d still feel depressed.
During these past eight months, has there been any stretch of more than two months when you felt mostly back to your normal self?

No… I don’t think so. It’s been kind of building and hanging around for about eight months now, since I took over that STEM-Arts curriculum initiative.

I mean, there are days where I can function better, or I get distracted by school things—assemblies, lesson prep, someone needing copies, all of that—but I wouldn’t say I’ve had more than two months where I felt like myself again. It hasn’t really lifted like that.
Have you been feeling worthless or overly guilty lately?

Yes… I have. Probably more than I want to admit.

It’s mostly with the curriculum project. If anything goes wrong—even something small, like a lesson not coming together right or people being confused—I immediately start thinking I’m letting the students down. And then my mind jumps to this whole other thing, like… my parents worked so hard and gave up so much so I could have opportunities, education, a stable job, all of that, and here I am messing it up.

I know that probably sounds dramatic, because it’s just a curriculum project, but in my head it feels bigger than that. Like I’m wasting what they sacrificed for.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energized or high and needed much less sleep than usual?

I’m not sure… I mean, I’ve had days where I push through and get a lot done, especially at school when there’s just no choice, like when everyone needs something at once and the copier jams—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

Unusually energized or high… I don’t think so? Not in a way that stands out to me. And the sleep part—I guess I’d need you to say more about what you mean by “needed” less sleep, because sometimes I stay up thinking about things, but that doesn’t feel like energy exactly.
Before this past eight months, was there ever a time in your life when you felt this same kind of depression for several months?

I’m… not really sure. I don’t think I have a clear memory of something like this lasting several months before, but it’s hard to compare, you know?

I’ve had difficult periods before—everyone has, I guess—and I can get caught up thinking about certain school years that were stressful, or family things, but I don’t know that it was the same as this. This feels… different enough that I’m having trouble saying yes or no confidently.
Before these past eight months, were there years when feeling down was just your usual baseline, even if it wasn’t as intense as this?

I don’t know if I’d say years, exactly… I mean, I’ve always had times where I’m more quiet or serious, and my husband would probably say I take things to heart too much. Even back when I first started working in classrooms, I remember feeling like I had to be cheerful for the kids, because you can’t exactly walk around looking miserable when a seven-year-old is showing you a drawing of a dinosaur or something.

But this… this feels more like most days there’s this heavy gray film over everything. Like I can be right in the middle of a classroom full of students, or sitting at home with my husband, and still feel hollow. Close to tears for no obvious reason. So I don’t know if that was my baseline before, but lately it’s been that way a lot.
Before these past eight months, was there ever a time when you felt depressed nearly every day for at least two weeks and it clearly got in the way of your life?

I’m trying to think of a specific time, and I’m not coming up with one clearly. There were definitely stretches where I felt low or overwhelmed, especially during busy school years, but “nearly every day for two weeks” and it really interfering… I don’t know.

It’s funny, because with school you just sort of keep showing up, you know? The kids still need help with their reading groups, someone still loses a mitten, there’s always some little crisis. So it’s hard for me to tell whether I was depressed in that way or just tired and stressed. I don’t remember a period before this that stands out as clearly getting in the way of my life like you’re asking.
Do these feelings seem stronger than you’d expect just from the school project stress?

Yes… I think so. I mean, the school project is stressful, definitely—there are always deadlines and people asking where things are, and somehow I end up remembering which kid needs construction paper or permission slips or whatever—but this feels bigger than that.

Most days it’s like there’s this heavy gray film over everything. I can be standing right there in a classroom full of students, with all that noise and movement, or at home with my husband, and I still feel hollow. Like I’m close to crying and I don’t even have a clear reason for it. So… yes, it feels stronger than just school stress.
Even on days when the school project isn’t especially stressful, do you still feel depressed?

Yes… even when the project is quiet for a day, or there isn’t some big deadline hanging over me, it’s still there.

I’ll be in the classroom and the kids are doing something perfectly normal—like arguing over crayons or showing me their handwriting—and I know I’m supposed to be present, but everything feels sort of covered over, like there’s this gray film between me and the room. Or I’ll be home with my husband, just sitting there, and I still feel hollow. Like I could cry, but there isn’t one clear thing I can point to and say, “That’s why.”

So yes, it’s not only on the stressful school days.
Have you noticed that your appetite has decreased lately?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear change, I guess. I mean, some days I don’t think about food much until my husband says something like, “Did you eat?” but other days I’ll eat normally enough.

It’s hard to tell because at school lunch is always rushed anyway—there’s barely time to sit down before someone needs help opening yogurt or there’s a spill—so I don’t know if that counts as appetite or just the day getting away from me. So… I wouldn’t say I’ve definitely noticed it decreasing.

doctor.question: Before these past eight months, was there ever a time when you felt depressed nearly every day for at least two weeks and it clearly got in the way of your life?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about any prior depressive episode before the current eight-month period, including duration and impairment. The provided symptom profile describes the current episode and does not cover past episodes.

patient.answer:
I’m trying to think of a specific time, and I’m not coming up with one clearly. There were definitely stretches where I felt low or overwhelmed, especially during busy school years, but “nearly every day for two weeks” and it really interfering… I don’t know.

It’s funny, because with school you just sort of keep showing up, you know? The kids still need help with their reading groups, someone still loses a mitten, there’s always some little crisis. So it’s hard for me to tell whether I was depressed in that way or just tired and stressed. I don’t remember a period before this that stands out as clearly getting in the way of my life like you’re asking.

doctor.intent: Differentiate major depressive disorder from adjustment disorder by determining whether the depressive symptoms are out of proportion to the identifiable stressor.
doctor.question: Do these feelings seem stronger than you’d expect just from the school project stress?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Most days I feel like there's a heavy gray film over everything, and I can be standing in a classroom full of students or at home with my husband and still feel hollow and close to tears.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the depressed feelings are disproportionate to the school project stress, which most directly relates to the persistent depressed mood.

patient.answer:
Yes… I think so. I mean, the school project is stressful, definitely—there are always deadlines and people asking where things are, and somehow I end up remembering which kid needs construction paper or permission slips or whatever—but this feels bigger than that.

Most days it’s like there’s this heavy gray film over everything. I can be standing right there in a classroom full of students, with all that noise and movement, or at home with my husband, and I still feel hollow. Like I’m close to crying and I don’t even have a clear reason for it. So… yes, it feels stronger than just school stress.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the depression is pervasively present across contexts rather than primarily tied to an identifiable stressor, to distinguish major depressive disorder from adjustment disorder with depressed mood.
doctor.question: Even on days when the school project isn’t especially stressful, do you still feel depressed?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Most days I feel like there's a heavy gray film over everything, and I can be standing in a classroom full of students or at home with my husband and still feel hollow and close to tears.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the depressed feeling persists even when the school project stress is lower, which directly concerns ongoing depressed mood.

patient.answer:
Yes… even when the project is quiet for a day, or there isn’t some big deadline hanging over me, it’s still there.

I’ll be in the classroom and the kids are doing something perfectly normal—like arguing over crayons or showing me their handwriting—and I know I’m supposed to be present, but everything feels sort of covered over, like there’s this gray film between me and the room. Or I’ll be home with my husband, just sitting there, and I still feel hollow. Like I could cry, but there isn’t one clear thing I can point to and say, “That’s why.”

So yes, it’s not only on the stressful school days.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the depression is causing a loss of appetite, which would further support a major depressive episode over adjustment disorder or persistent depressive disorder.
doctor.question: Have you noticed that your appetite has decreased lately?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about decreased appetite, but the provided symptom profile does not include an appetite or weight-change item.

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear change, I guess. I mean, some days I don’t think about food much until my husband says something like, “Did you eat?” but other days I’ll eat normally enough.

It’s hard to tell because at school lunch is always rushed anyway—there’s barely time to sit down before someone needs help opening yogurt or there’s a spill—so I don’t know if that counts as appetite or just the day getting away from me. So… I wouldn’t say I’ve definitely noticed it decreasing.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a current depressive episode lasting about 8 months with depressed mood, marked loss of interest, insomnia, guilt/worthlessness, passive death wishes, and clear functional impairment at work and home. Symptoms are present even when the school stressor is quiet and feel disproportionate to that stressor, supporting a depressive episode rather than adjustment disorder. Recurrent depressive disorder is not established because prior qualifying episodes cannot be confirmed. Persistent mood disorder/dysthymia is not supported because a chronic multi-year depressive baseline before the current episode was not established.
